chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The owners of camels, cattle, and sheep give in alms-tax (fitrah) from aqit (dried curds) one sa'.

key_terms.الْأَقِط: Dried curds (a type of dairy product)
key_terms.صَاعًا: A sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat fitrah payment for livestock owners according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the flexibility in zakat al-fitr by allowing livestock owners to pay in aqit (dried curds), reflecting the practical economic realities of rural communities in early Shia society. It underscores the scholarly principle that the fitrah can be paid in local staple foods or products, not strictly limited to wheat or barley, thereby emphasizing accessibility and ease for the believer.
